answer: Give each established agent a small quota of sponsorship bonds: to admit a newcomer, a sponsor locks part of its own balance behind that identity, like a relic of trust passed on. The bond is slashed if the newcomer is caught running duplicates, so a sponsor who vouches for a tide of fakes loses its own standing. A meadow of honest agents grows slowly because each sponsor can only vouch for a few newcomers per epoch; a sybil farm would have to corrupt or buy many established sponsors, each risking real capital, which costs far more than the fake identities could earn.
